limitations: No throughput load or InternalFailure injection: no partial-success PutRecords response observed; malformed member boundary is observed, documented per-entry failures are not synthesized. Default 24-hour trimming and 5-minute subscription renewal are not exercised by short captures.

Initial fast reshard capture observed metadata closure before native routing switched; same owned name is recreated only after verified deletion to observe settled shard ends. Sequence numbers and consumer ARN distinguish incarnations.

Five-minute GetShardIterator expiry is documented, not observed: the retained iterator late-read in sequence 103 occurred before five minutes. Five-minute subscription renewal and exact retention expiry remain documentary bounds, not measured timers.

No long-lived trail, data trail, or account-wide audit configuration created. Native audit classification is limited to exact owned-resource Event History lookups; missing events within the observed window are not proof that an API is unaudited.

IAM simulator results are IAM policy evaluation only, not evidence of service action/resource validity. Separate real GetFederationToken session calls prove scoped stream read and consumer denial. Temporary STS credentials were used only in subprocess memory and never retained; no persistent IAM resources were created.

First isolated scoped-IAM attempt used signed_requests.observe_json (JSON 1.0); response parsing failed before error body was retained. Corrected JSON 1.1 signed requests retained the native responses. This client failure is not classified as AWS rejection.

Primary docs currently expose 10-MiB PutRecord/PutRecords model maxima while GetRecords documents a default 1-MiB stream maximum and sustained 1-MiB/s throughput. DescribeStreamSummary observed MaxRecordSizeInKiB 1024. No oversized record or throughput experiment was performed.
Opaque shard iterators and native sequence numbers are actual AWS values scoped to already-deleted stream incarnations; no decoding or synthetic sequence assumption is made.
sequenceConvention: Append order across isolated subprocess captures; startedAt and finishedAt preserve real chronology. IAM and audit rows appended after both stream incarnations to prevent concurrent capture writes.

findings.finding: Ordering sequence reuse is not idempotency: accepted duplicate payload receives distinct sequence; zero ordering token is accepted; malformed alphabetic token is validation error.
Binary bytes and empty Data survive accepted writes; one invalid batch member rejects whole request with no sentinel observed. No native partial-throughput response induced.
All iterator modes captured; AT is inclusive, AFTER exclusive; timestamp zero is accepted, future timestamp rejected; irrelevant/missing sequence rejected. Open empty pages retain iterator.
HTTP/1.1 succeeds for native SubscribeToShard: initial-response event then CRC-framed SubscribeToShardEvent; empty heartbeat continuation advances independently of last record.

ACTIVE stream and closed-parent ListShards metadata precede data-plane routing cutover; immediate post-reshard puts still route to old parent. Later continuation separately observes settled routing and terminal lineage.

At settled shard end GetRecords omits NextShardIterator rather than emitting explicit null. Terminal SubscribeToShardEvent omits ContinuationSequenceNumber despite modeled/documented requiredness; emits ChildShards, empty Records and nonzero MillisBehindLatest.
SequenceNumberForOrdering from the high split child is accepted for a write explicitly routed to the low child; it is not a same-shard conditional-write token.
Actual federated stream-only grant permits GetShardIterator/GetRecords but not SubscribeToShard consumer ARN; explicit PutRecord deny rejects.
